chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, raising it (mursal), from Muhammad ibn Humran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created four containers for the womb. So whatever was in the first is (similar to) the father, and whatever was in the second is (similar to) the mother, and whatever was in the third is (similar to) the paternal uncles, and whatever was in the fourth is (similar to) the maternal uncles.

key_terms.أوعية: Containers/vessels (awʿiya) — the four zones or compartments believed to determine the child's resemblance
key_terms.الخؤولة: Maternal uncles (khūʾūla) — the maternal side of extended family
key_terms.الرحم: The womb (rahim) — central to discussions of lineage, birth, and kinship in fiqh
key_terms.العمومة: Paternal uncles (ʿumūma) — the paternal side of extended family
key_terms.رفعه: Mursal (marfūʿ) — the chain is raised/elevated, indicating a break, making this a mursal hadith

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the four containers of the womb and family resemblance?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) describes a cosmological-biological teaching about the womb, stating that Allah created four 'containers' (vessels or zones) within the womb. The offspring's resemblance is determined by which container they developed in: the first yields resemblance to the father, the second to the mother, the third to paternal uncles, and the fourth to maternal uncles. This hadith reflects early Islamic embryological concepts and was used in jurisprudential discussions on lineage and resemblance.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Muhammad, raising it, from Muhammad Bin Humran, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Created four containers for the womb. So whatever was in the first, so it is (similar to) the father, and whatever was in the second, so it is (similar to) the mother, and whatever was in the third so it is (similar to) the paternal uncles, and whatever was in the fourth, so it is (similar to) the maternal uncles’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from in a marfu ‘ manner from Muhammad ibn Humran who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

Allah has created four receptacles for the womb. Whatever is from the first is for the father, whatever is from the second is from the mother, whatever is from the third is from the paternal uncles and whatever is from the fourth is from the maternal uncles (in gender or shape).’”
